fields.title: What Should Be Logged
fields.keyTakeaway: Action logs record logins, permissions, access to personal data, exports, and supplier actions, must be technically tamper-evident, and their transparency to the client is a sales argument.
fields.sections/0/blocks/0/text: A client asks: "which of our employees exported the buyer database in March?" Can we answer?
fields.sections/1/blocks/0/text: The absence of a log makes investigation, mandatory reporting, and dispute resolution impossible. This question usually arises at the moment when the log is already gone and the event has already happened.
fields.sections/2/blocks/0/text: **[[audit-log|Audit log]]** differs from technical logs: it is about who did what, not about what happened in the system.
fields.sections/2/blocks/2/text: *Who.* Subject identifier, including when our employee acts on behalf of the client. *What.* Action type and object. *When.* Time accurate to the second. *From where.* Address, device — for investigations. *Result.* Success or denial. Denials matter: a series of denials is a sign of probing.
fields.sections/2/blocks/3/text: What actions get into the log:
fields.sections/2/blocks/4/text: **Mandatory:** login and logout, permission changes, access to personal data in volume, exports and data dumps, security settings changes, data deletion, our support actions on behalf of the client.
fields.sections/2/blocks/5/text: **As appropriate:** viewing individual records — the volume can be huge; changes to regular data.
fields.sections/2/blocks/6/text: Key property — **[[tamper-evidence|tamper evidence]]**: a record cannot be changed or deleted, and this must be ensured technically, not by a rule. A log that an administrator can edit is useless for an investigation.
fields.sections/2/blocks/7/text: Second — **retention period**. Questionnaires usually require 6–12 months. This is a separate line in retention and separate expenses.
fields.sections/3/blocks/0/text: Logged events: logins, changes to employee roster and permissions, all exports, viewing the buyer list, changing store settings, our support actions.
fields.sections/3/blocks/1/text: Viewing an individual order is not logged — the volume would be larger than the orders themselves. Compromise: records the fact of opening the personal data section and the number of records viewed per session.
fields.sections/3/blocks/2/text: This compromise — a product decision, discussed: full traceability versus volume. Volume won, with the caveat that a full mode is possible for the enterprise tier.
fields.sections/3/blocks/3/text: The log is available to the client in the account: filters by employee, action, period. Export to file.
fields.sections/3/blocks/4/text: Separate entry — actions by our support. The partner sees that a Polka employee accessed their account, when and for which ticket. This proved to be a strong argument in negotiations: transparency instead of promises.
fields.sections/4/blocks/0/text: The log itself contains personal data and follows the same rules: access to it is restricted, retention period is defined, account deletion affects it — with caveats for legally required records.
fields.sections/5/blocks/0/text: Action logs record logins, permissions, access to personal data, exports, and supplier actions, must be technically tamper-evident, and their transparency to the client is a sales argument.
